accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:deterministic-rate-limit and the local minimax envelope theorems
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The procedure class is restricted to pilot-adaptive procedures whose main-wave annotation rates converge locally uniformly to a deterministic feasible design.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All lower, upper, and attainment claims are conditional on the deterministic-limit class A_det; they do not cover sequential, positive-fraction-pilot, or random-limit designs.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops limit-of-experiments approximations for statistical treatment assignment and derives asymptotically optimal rules under average and minimax risk criteria.

The paper optimizes annotation probabilities for ATE variance, gives a closed-form solution, and states that a feasible two-batch estimator attains the best asymptotic variance; its comments identify an AISTATS 2026 preliminary version.
The source labels the paper Preprint and Status FUTURE, while describing a maximin semiparametric-efficiency criterion for scalar or multidimensional two-phase parameters.
The published paper studies adaptive-treatment ATE inference and provides a semiparametrically efficient adaptive AIPW CLT.

The preprint designs a second experimental wave for Bayes-regret policy choice using Gaussian and local-quadratic approximations, with local strong-concavity/uniqueness regularity used in its asymptotic result.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Manski studies minimax-regret treatment choice with missing outcomes and includes randomized-experiment dropout as a motivating missing-data setting; it does not solve prospective randomized annotation design.
The article studies double sampling for missing data in causal ATE analysis and develops observed-data influence-function based estimators under its double-sampling assumptions.
The paper studies minimax-regret sample selection for heterogeneous randomized trials and derives allocation schemes, rather than the proposed selective-outcome overlapping-policy covariance problem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the undefined experiment-convergence phrase with an explicit conditional LAN expansion and a precise projected-score or Le Cam-risk-transfer statement, then give an effective input encoding for H and all certified numerical primitives.

Add Manski (2007) and Stoye’s missing-outcome minimax-regret results to related work, stating explicitly why random annotation, point identification, overlapping policy loadings, and design optimization evade their settings.

Either compare G to a named published multivariate two-phase design criterion with an exact formula, or reframe the witness as an internal geometric phenomenon rather than a refutation of a standard variance-design workflow.
